SOURCE: "Neural Computers", Mingchen Zhuge, Changsheng Zhao, Haozhe Liu, Zijian Zhou, Shuming Liu, Wenyi Wang, Ernie Chang, Gael Le Lan, Junjie Fei, Wenxuan Zhang, Yasheng Sun, Zhipeng Cai, Zechun Liu, Yunyang Xiong, Yining Yang, Yuandong Tian, Yangyang Shi, Vikas Chandra, Jürgen Schmidhuber. Meta AI and KAUST. arXiv 2604.06425v2 [cs.LG], preprint (no venue). The PDF header stamps v2 as 16 Apr 2026, but the title block says "Date: April 20, 2026". The two dates disagree and I do not know which is right. Local file: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/02-context-engineering/sources/zhuge-2026-neural-computers.pdf

COVERAGE: Read 0 to about 130,000 of 163,781 chars. That covers the main text (pp.1-28), the references (skimmed), and Appendices A, B, C and D. Appendix E (about chars 150,000 to the end) is only figure pages of rollout screenshots with no results text. I read its intro and the last pages, and skipped the middle. Extraction was clean. No scanned or garbled pages.

VERDICT ON FIT: Weak and mostly off-topic for context engineering. It is a position and vision paper with a small video-model prototype. It has no LLM context-window, retrieval, memory-management or prompt-budget experiments. The only links are conceptual: runtime state as working memory, a run/update separation, install-reuse, and conditioning or specification quality. For a speculative-track note it is usable as a "what might come after context windows" pointer. It is not evidence for any context-engineering practice. Much of the paper is a manifesto, and the authors label the Section 4.4 remarks "hypotheses ... rather than empirical conclusions".

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Definition: a Neural Computer folds compute, memory and I/O into one latent runtime state h_t, updated and rendered in a loop.
  number: none
  setup: formalism for the video-model prototypes (Wan2.1 backbone). h_t is realized as the diffusion model's video latents z_t.
  quote: "ht =F θ(ht−1, xt, ut), x t+1 ∼G θ(ht)." and "ht provides the persistent runtime memory,Fθ carries the state-update computation"
  where: p.3, Eq. 2.1
- The paper contrasts NCs with agents. In agents, executable state lives outside the model. In an NC, the learned runtime is the machine.
  number: none
  quote: "they are not a smarter layer on top of the existing stack, but a proposal to make the model itself the running computer."
  where: p.2. Table 13 on p.23 gives the four-way comparison (conventional computer, AI agent, world model, NC).
- Proposed run/update contract for a future "Completely Neural Computer" (CNC). This is the only part that connects to harness and context ideas. It is a hypothesis and untested.
  number: none
  quote: "Run: invoke installed capability without silently changing persistent behavior. • Update: any behavior-changing modification should occur explicitly through a programming interface." Boundaries: "state (what persists), update (what counts as reprogramming), and evidence (what can be replayed, compared, or rolled back)."
  where: p.24, Section 4.2. Also three "acceptance lenses" on p.22: "install–reuse, execution consistency, and update governance".
- The authors hypothesize that gating (as in LSTM) could give the run/update separation. They also say unbounded effective memory is needed for Turing completeness.
  number: none
  quote: "We hypothesize that gating mechanisms, such as those in LSTM (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber, 1997), are effective in achieving this conditional invariance." and "For an NC instance to achieve universality, unbounded effective memory is necessary."
  where: p.24
- Reprompting raised CLI arithmetic accuracy from 4% to 83%. The authors say this shows steerability, not native computation.
  number: 4% to 83%
  setup: NCCLIGen (Wan2.1-based) on CLIGen (Clean) arithmetic probes. The probe set is 100 problems sampled from a held-out pool of 1,000. The backbone is unchanged and there is no RL. In roughly half the training captions the correct answer is included in the caption. The reprompt supplies the answer as a hint (Figs 23-25 show "The answer is 5").
  quote: "NCCLIGen accuracy on CLIGen (Clean) arithmetic tasks rises from 4% to 83% under reprompting." and "Much of the apparent "reasoning" gain can come from better specification and instruction-following rather than new native computation." and "We do not treat it as a clean demonstration that the NC backbone performs arithmetic internally."
  where: p.10, Exp. 6. Fig. 6.
- Arithmetic probe baselines: native symbolic computation is poor in video models.
  number: Wan2.1 0%, NCCLIGen 4%, Veo3.1 2%, Sora2 71%
  setup: same 100-problem probe. The reason for Sora2's result is unknown. Table 6 lists three hypotheses (stronger base, extra RL, system-level reprompt or LLM) and does not test them.
  quote: "Wan2.1 achieves 0% accuracy, our NCCLIGen model reaches 4%, and Veo3.1 manages 2%" and "Sora2's 71% accuracy is a notable outlier"
  where: p.10, Table 5
- More literal captions give better rendering.
  number: PSNR 21.90 dB (semantic, 55 words), 23.63 (regular, 52 words), 26.89 (detailed, 76 words). SSIM 0.813, 0.843, 0.867.
  setup: CLIGen (General) TI2V fidelity, same underlying terminal sequences, three Llama-3.1-70B-generated caption styles.
  quote: "PSNR increases from 21.90 dB (semantic) to 26.89 dB (detailed), a gain of nearly 5 dB"
  where: p.9, Table 3. The authors' interpretation: "Detailed captions act as scaffolding".
- A small amount of goal-directed data beat much larger random exploration for GUI action-response learning.
  number: FVD_all 14.72 (Claude CUA, about 110 h), 20.37 (Random Slow, about 1,000 h), 48.17 (Random Fast, about 400 h), 149.61 (untrained). SSIM_all 0.885, 0.830, 0.695, 0.496.
  setup: NCGUIWorld under contextual conditioning. Ubuntu 22.04 and XFCE desktop at 1024x768 and 15 FPS. The three training sets differ in source as well as size, and the split they are evaluated on is not stated in the text I read. It is an open-loop comparison.
  quote: "data quality matters more than dataset size for action-driven performance"
  where: p.17, Table 8
- Cursor accuracy needs explicit visual supervision.
  number: 8.7% (position only), 13.5% (position + Fourier), 98.7% (position + SVG mask/reference)
  setup: GUIWorld. 98.7% is described as holding "under explicit supervision in controlled settings".
  quote: "Under this explicit visual conditioning, cursor accuracy improves to 98.7%."
  where: p.17-18, Table 9
- Deeper action injection works better than input-level conditioning.
  number: SSIM+15 / LPIPS+15 / FVD+15: external 0.746 / 0.251 / 33.4; contextual 0.813 / 0.190 / 24.8; residual 0.857 / 0.138 / 18.8; internal 0.863 / 0.141 / 14.5.
  setup: 15 frames after each action, same data and encoder. The external baseline was early-stopped at about 50% of its training budget, so that comparison is not like for like. Training ran about 64k steps per mode.
  quote: "internal achieves the highest structural consistency (SSIM 0.863) and the lowest temporal distortion (FVD 14.5), while residual attains the lowest perceptual distance (LPIPS 0.138)."
  where: p.18, Table 10
- Action encoding matters less than injection depth.
  number: raw-action 0.847 / 0.144 / 16.6 vs meta-action 0.863 / 0.141 / 14.5 (SSIM+15 / LPIPS+15 / FVD+15)
  quote: "encoding granularity is secondary to alignment quality and injection strategy"
  where: p.18-19, Table 11
- CLI text rendering is learnable but modest. OCR accuracy plateaus, and global metrics flatten early.
  number: character accuracy 0.03 at step 0 rising to 0.54 at 60k steps. Exact-line accuracy 0.01 rising to 0.31. Average PSNR 40.77 and SSIM 0.989 for VAE reconstruction at a 13px font. PSNR/SSIM plateau around 25k steps (run to 460k).
  setup: CLIGen (Clean), Tesseract OCR on 5 frames per video. Training cost about 15,000 H100 hours for General and about 7,000 for Clean. GUIWorld runs cost about 23k GPU-hours per pass.
  quote: "Character accuracy increases from 0.03 at initialization to 0.54 at 60k steps, with exact-line matches reaching 0.31 (0.26 by 40k)."
  where: pp.9-10, Table 4. VAE numbers on p.8, Table 2.
- Data scale. CLIGen (General) is 823,989 clips (about 1,100 h). CLIGen (Clean) is about 250k scripts with 51.21% kept, giving about 78k regular and about 50k Python-math traces.
  quote: "The resulting 823,989 video streams (approximately 1,100 hours) are resampled to 15 FPS."
  where: p.5-7
- The authors' own summary of what works and what does not:
  quote: "NCs have begun to exhibit early runtime primitives—most notably I/O alignment and short-horizon control—while stable reuse, symbolic reliability, and runtime governance remain unresolved."
  where: p.28

LIMITS
- No experiment tests reuse, install-reuse, long-horizon consistency, update governance, or capability retention. These are the paper's central claims for a CNC, and all are roadmap items.
- Evaluation is open-loop, replaying logged prompts and actions. Quote: "evaluation remains open-loop rather than closed-loop interaction with a live environment" (p.4).
- Single backbone (Wan2.1), with no baselines other than untrained models and the closed models in the arithmetic probe. The arithmetic probe is small (100 problems) and has no confidence intervals. I saw no seeds or variance anywhere in the text.
- The authors concede that symbolic stability is a bottleneck and that the video-model substrate is "pragmatic rather than fundamental" (p.27).
- The CNC definition (Turing complete, universally programmable, behavior-consistent, machine-native) is not demonstrated. The finite-precision caveat on Turing completeness is conceded (p.24). The "machine-native architecture" and "neural network generation via NC interaction" remarks are labelled conjecture.
- The paper says no more about its weaker experiments than is quoted above. The "metadata" release claims ("released configs") were not verified.
- Dated: it depends on Wan2.1 and compares to Veo 3.1, Sora 2, Genie 3 and NeuralOS, as of early 2026.

BUILDS ON
Ha and Schmidhuber 2018 (World Models); NeuralOS (Rivard et al., 2025), whose cursor representation and data pipeline they adopt; Wan2.1 (Wan et al., 2025); Genie / Genie 3 (Bruce et al., 2024); Veo 3.1 and Sora 2; Imagine with Claude (Anthropic, 2025); Claude computer-use agent for the supervised GUI data; Neural Turing Machines (Graves et al., 2014); Differentiable Neural Computers (Graves et al., 2016); Neural Programmer-Interpreters (Reed and De Freitas, 2015); Schmidhuber fast weight programmers (1992, 1993) and "One Big Net for Everything" (2018); ControlNet (Zhang et al., 2023, for the residual mode); Matrix-Game-2 (He et al., 2025, for the internal mode); Siegelmann and Sontag 1992 (neural Turing completeness); LSTM (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber, 1997); Wiedemer et al., 2025 (video models as zero-shot reasoners).

CODE: none worth keeping. Appendix C.1/C.2 gives an asciinema .cast sample and a vhs script format (p.41-43). Only the Eq. 2.1 loop on p.3 is of conceptual use.

FIGURES (not rendered; captions taken from the text)
- Teaser, p.1: classical computer (compute/memory/I/O modules) set against a neural latent stack where h_t covers all three. Fastest summary of the thesis.
- Fig. 6, p.10: "Reprompting boosts performance to 83%". Shows the 4% to 83% result.
- Fig. 7, p.15: four action-injection modes (external, contextual, residual, internal).
- Fig. 9, p.26: "Changing human-machine relations across conventional computers, the agent era, and neural computers". It places agents between the user and an existing computer, and an NC as the learned runtime itself.
- Table 13, p.23: system-object comparison, useful if the note needs the agent vs NC distinction.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found in the text.
- The PDF's date is ambiguous (16 Apr vs 20 Apr 2026).
- The reference list contains a duplicate entry (Zhuge et al. 2026a and 2026b are identical, "AI with recursive self-improvement", ICLR 2026 Workshop Proposals). The Wei et al. chain-of-thought paper is listed twice (2022 and 2023). A Kingma and Ba entry is garbled as "Adam et al." These are minor.
- The paper uses "reasoning" and "runtime" loosely. Do not cite its 83% as evidence of reasoning ability. The paper itself says not to.
- For the note: cite it only for the framing (runtime state as memory, run/update separation, acceptance lenses) and the reprompting caveat. It is a "sharpens" candidate at most. It supports nothing about context windows.
